properties.description:

rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 3 inches of rain have
fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 2.5 to 3.5 inches in 1 hour.
Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Grandfalls, Imperial Reservoir, Royalty and Fort Stockton-Pecos
County Airport.

Comanche Creek, Pecos River and Leon Creek.

deaths occur in vehicles.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Washita River near Clinton.

* WHEN...From this afternoon to Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 19.0 feet, Approximately one thousand acres of rural
lands are covered by depths up to a foot... from areas near the
mouth of Barnitz Creek... to near Clinton in Custer County... and
downstream to near the town of Cloud Chief in Washita County.
greater depths may be confined to small areas where local streams
enter the Washita River valley. Some farmsteads may be flooded or
isolated by water over local roads. Some farm levees may be
overtopped.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 18.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 18.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 1:30 PM CDT Wednesday was 18.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 19.1 feet
this evening. It will then fall below flood stage tomorrow
morning.
- Flood stage is 18.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 300 AM CDT.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 14 at 9:36AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...Forecast flooding changed from Minor to Moderate severity for the
following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.The St Johns River at Astor is forecast to remain in Minor Flood
Stage through Friday, as previous heavy rainfall continues to drain
through the basin. However, strong northeasterly winds this weekend
are forecast to lead a return to Moderate Flood Stage.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon
Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water
approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and
Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river
water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor
Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are
covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud
roads are underwater with yards inundated. At 3.0 feet, Water
approaches or may enter lowest homes on or near Wildhog Road and
nearby canals. Flooding reaches the parking lot of the Juno Trail
Apartments. Flooding on portions of Alligator Road and Holiday
Road. Lowest lying yards along Blue Creek are flooded. Roads at
Astor Landing Campground and Lake Dexter Boat Ramp begin to flood.
Water enters lower homes closest to the river on McPherson Lane.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EDT Wednesday was 2.9 feet.

stage at 2.8 feet.

- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
